findings.reason: the repair should promote the existing private primitive and route both forks through it, not describe an addition; this changes the node's file list and its surface accounting.
findings.text: §8 says the owner "gains a bytes-payload path" so a call site staging non-JSON bytes need not keep its own replace, but `_write_through_sibling_temporary(path, render, *, fsync, mode, fsync_directory)` already performs exactly that: it writes any payload a caller's `render(handle)` callable produces through a unique sibling temporary, and `write_json_atomically` is itself only a thin adapter over it (`reckon/_store.py:511`)

findings.reason: the honest move is to extend the owner (pass the line-log as a render callback) rather than keep a second writer beside it; the plan's §8 currently leaves this fork.
findings.text: `_replace_atomically`'s docstring keeps it "rather than moved onto the shared JSON writer" because the pane history is a log of JSON lines one commit of the document-oriented writer cannot express; that reason is valid against `write_json_atomically` alone, but not against the owner's `_write_through_sibling_temporary`, which expresses the line-log directly, so the retained wrapper is justified against the wrong mechanism

findings.reason: §8 declares a single durable-replace owner but its own check cannot see this fork; the done-when should also require that the directory-fsync be single-homed in the owner, or the same defect the section exists to close is left one level down.
findings.text: `_fsync_directory` here is a byte-for-byte second copy of `reckon/_store.py:367:_fsync_directory`, and §8's done-when greps only `def _durable_replace\|def _replace_atomically`, so this lower-level duplicate survives the repair even after `_durable_replace` is retired

findings.reason: §8's premise that two forks "survived" is an undercount visible in the owner module itself; the design should fold this third replace path in or name why it is exempt, otherwise the section's census-grep done-when passes while the mechanism is still copied, which is the same instrument blind spot §8 was written to correct.
findings.text: the evidence-append path writes `path.with_suffix(".html.tmp")` then `tmp.replace(path)` inside `_store.py` itself, bypassing `_write_through_sibling_temporary`, so "one atomic writer" is false within the very module §8 names as the owner

findings.reason: the section's interface accounting is incorrect as written and must state the real delta (zero on retirement, and a surface addition if a new public entry point is introduced), which is the accounting rule §5 exists to enforce.
findings.text: §8 states "the public_definitions family shrinks by the two retired forks", but `_durable_replace` and `_replace_atomically` are underscore-private and `reckon/interface_counts.py:82-91` marks a definition public only when it and its enclosing classes are all non-underscore (verified directly: the counter reports `_durable_replace` public=False, and project_state.py reads 24 public / 47 non-public definitions), so retiring them moves public_definitions by nothing; if the owner instead gains a *public* bytes entry point the family grows by one

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §7 and §8 add no new module; the depth already lives in `reckon/_store.py`, and the repair preserves it if it promotes the existing private primitive rather than adding a second public adapter.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `reckon/project_state.py:_fsync_directory` is a second copy of the owner's own `_fsync_directory`, invisible to §8's own done-when grep, and `reckon/_store.py` contains a third replace path beside the primitive it names.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 claims the public_definitions family shrinks by the two retired forks, but both names are underscore-private and the counter counts only non-underscore definitions, so the family cannot move and the section's accounting is wrong as written.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §8 declares the owner will "gain a bytes-payload path", but `reckon/_store.py:_write_through_sibling_temporary` already is that generic payload path.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py:_replace_atomically` is retained with a justification that argues against `write_json_atomically` but not against the owner's render-callback primitive.
